title: Liam Coen Recaps Loss to Giants in Week 11 | Press Conference
headline: Coen blames himself for a sloppy 23-18 loss to the Giants: red zone play-calling, a failed fourth-and-1 pass, and a new center. Josh Cameron was open on that play, and Coen says he'll run the ball more in the red zone.
summary: Coen opened by saying the team was not prepared well enough and put that directly on himself. He pointed to 13 penalties to the Giants' six, many of them pre-snap, and tied some to a new center in the lineup (Jonah Monheim) and trying to anticipate silent counts on the road against strong pass rushers. He called his red zone plan a mistake: after calling bad runs the previous week at Tennessee, he leaned pass-heavy and now says they should have run more. The offense went 1-for-6 in the red zone, and he said the run game was ineffective early, which put them in second-and-long and third-and-long. On the late fourth-and-1 from the 11, he said Jacksonville had the right look but missed the read to Josh Cameron, who was open. Coen explained that the earlier decision to kick a field goal while trailing was driven by the analytics charts, which favored kicking and getting a stop. He said Trevor Lawrence competed hard and gave them a chance, though Lawrence threw a number of 50-50 balls, partly because of pressure, with Parker Washington on the receiving end of a few. Coen said the defense didn't play great early but held the Giants to 23 points, and that the team lacked complementary football and special teams play, concluding they were outplayed and outcoached.

signals.claim: Cameron was open on the key fourth-and-1 and the read to him was missed; he is a possible target in short-yardage and red zone calls.
signals.note: Coen said he was open on a critical red zone fourth down, so he could see short-yardage or red zone looks.
signals.quote: just missing the read to Josh Cameron was was, you know, quite open there

signals.claim: Lawrence will be reviewed on tape for the 50-50 throws, but Coen thinks he competed and gave the team a chance.
signals.note: Coen backed his QB despite pressure and contested throws, so there is no sign of a role change.
signals.quote: Trevor, I thought he competed his tail off. He gave us a chance to win.

signals.claim: Washington was a frequent target on contested 50-50 balls, partly because Lawrence was pressured and trying to give him opportunities after big plays last week.
signals.note: He is getting targets, but many were contested, which adds volatility.

signals.claim: Monheim started at center in place of the injured Robert Hainsey, and Coen said he was not at fault for the penalties.
signals.note: Line continuity is a concern with Hainsey out, which affects pass protection and the run game.

topics.detail: Jacksonville was flagged 13 times to the Giants' six, with a number of pre-snap penalties from silent counts and a motion Coen wasn't sure about.
The team went 1-for-6 in the red zone. Coen said he went too pass-heavy after last week's bad runs and should have run more.
Coen explained the earlier field goal as a chart-driven choice and said the late fourth-and-1 pass failed because of a missed read, not the call.
The defense forced turnovers that the offense did not turn into points, and special teams and field position were poor.

title: Head Coach Jim Harbaugh Postgame Press Conference vs. Jets
headline: Chargers fall one field goal short to the Jets; Harbaugh gives no injury or role news, but says the offense ran well, was efficient on third down, and needs faster tempo on the final drive.
summary: Harbaugh opened by saying he was disappointed the Chargers didn't get the win. He kept most answers general and said the staff would study the tape. He said the offense ran the ball pretty well, was efficient on third down and didn't turn it over. He also said the team needs to finish drives with touchdowns rather than field goals. He was critical of the defense and said it couldn't force turnovers or get enough stops, and he acknowledged the Jets were very good on first and third down, mostly converting short yardage, and ran effectively without punting. On the final offensive drive, which took about six minutes, he said the team should have gone faster and that he is stressing operation speed and tempo with the players and with Mike. Asked whether the quarterback bore some of the blame, he defended Justin Herbert, saying the offense took what the defense gave it and was very efficient. Asked about fans and the future, he said the team will keep working and offered no further assurances. He gave no injury updates and no depth chart or role changes.

signals.claim: Herbert played efficiently and took what the defense gave him; no blame placed on him for the final drive's pace.
signals.note: The coach backs Herbert and the offense's efficiency, so no sign of a quarterback or scheme change; the main issue is tempo and finishing drives in the end zone.
signals.quote: took what the defense gave us

topics.detail: Harbaugh said the offense ran the ball pretty well, was efficient on third down and didn't turn it over. The emphasis is on finishing drives with touchdowns.
The final drive took about six minutes and ended in a field goal. Harbaugh wants faster operation speed and says he is pushing it with the players and with Mike.
The Jets converted on first and third downs, mostly in short yardage, ran effectively and never punted. The Chargers couldn't force turnovers or get enough stops.
Neither team is headed to the playoffs, and Harbaugh gave no specifics beyond continuing to work and focusing on next Sunday.

title: Klint Kubiak Postgame Presser - 11.22.26 | Week 11
headline: Brock Bowers sat out Week 11 but Kubiak is optimistic and says he's making progress, while Jack Bech and Jalen Nailor stepped up in his absence and Ashton Jeanty remains a featured piece.
summary: Kubiak opened by reporting that Tim Keenan has an MCL injury and that JJ Pegues and Adam Butler left the game, with Butler in concussion territory. Rookie QB Fernando Mendoza made his second start on the road in a very loud stadium. He started shakily, including a burned timeout, but improved as the game went on, and Kubiak praised his leadership and said he has shown he can run the operation. Kubiak now wants him to cut turnovers and put up more points. The Raiders had nine penalties after zero the week before, which Kubiak called unacceptable. Six passes were batted down, and he plans to check the tape, starting with the quarterback's eyes. Brock Bowers was held out on a group medical decision because he wasn't ready, but Kubiak said he is optimistic and Bowers is making progress. With Bowers out, Jalen Nailor and Jack Bech had to step up, and Bech had a standout day despite some drops overall. The run game worked through persistence, and Kubiak singled out Ashton Jeanty as continuing to make plays. The defensive tackle room is badly depleted, and Kubiak called it difficult but said other players get opportunities.

injuries.detail: Kubiak said he has an MCL injury; no timeline was given.
Came out of the game; Kubiak gave no diagnosis.
Came out of the game with a concussion.
Did not play on a group medical decision because he was not ready. Kubiak is optimistic and says he is making progress. A reporter mentioned a possible return against Cleveland.
A reporter said he was already out, leaving the team down four defensive tackles. Kubiak did not address his status.

signals.claim: Bowers is progressing and could return soon, possibly against Cleveland.
signals.note: Bowers is trending toward a return but is not confirmed, so check the injury report before setting lineups.
signals.quote: I am optimistic, yes. He's making progress.

signals.claim: Bech gets more targets when Bowers is out and produced his best game as a pro.
signals.note: Bech is a short-term pass-catching option while Bowers is sidelined and could lose work when Bowers returns.
signals.quote: he makes those plays in practice

signals.claim: Nailor was among the receivers who stepped up in Bowers' absence.
signals.note: He gets a bigger target share when Bowers is out, though drops were a team issue.
signals.quote: those guys had to step up and I thought they did.

signals.claim: Jeanty will keep leading the run game after a productive day.
signals.note: The ground game worked, a 68-yard touchdown was a spark, and Kubiak singled out Jeanty as a leader and playmaker.
signals.quote: I think Ashton is continuing to make to make plays.

signals.claim: Mendoza remains the starting QB and must cut turnovers and score more.
signals.note: He is improving but still shaky, with early struggles, an interception and six batted passes, so his fantasy ceiling is unproven.
signals.quote: I've learned that he can run the operation

topics.detail: Nine penalties after zero the previous week. Kubiak called it unacceptable and said the team can't win that way.
Keenan, Pegues and Butler all left the game, leaving the position very thin. Kubiak said young players have to be ready for their next snap.
Six passes were batted down, and Kubiak will study the tape, focusing on Mendoza's eyes. He called the interception a good play by Denver and a poor call by himself.
Kubiak credited persistence and the halfbacks for the run game's success, and noted the pads-day practice, saying he'd do pads daily if allowed.

title: Coach John Harbaugh: ‘This is where the season starts’
headline: Giants beat the Jaguars behind a dominant defense: Abdul Carter had 12 pressures, Paulson Adebo had a standout game, and J.J. McCarthy still has to hit his deep shots.
summary: Harbaugh called the Week 11 win over the Jaguars a "real football win" and said the season effectively starts now. He praised the defense, especially the corners, Abdul Carter, Kayvon Thibodeaux and a defensive line that shut down the run. He said the offense moved the ball well except for penalties, and that it missed a chance to put the game away early in the third quarter with a missed kick, a failed touchdown opportunity and a turnover. Paulson Adebo got a game ball and was called a legitimate corner, even though he was inactive the week before. Carter's 12 pressures were singled out, and Harbaugh said he sensed the breakout coming from how Carter practices. Harbaugh defended trusting his ball carrier late despite an earlier fumble, citing the team's emphasis on ball security. He credited J.J. McCarthy's late throw to Malachi Fields as a big-time play, admitted the deep passing game was inconsistent, and said those shots will start connecting. He closed by stressing the need to stack wins against a hungry opponent next week.

injuries.detail: Harbaugh said he worked through an injury, got in great shape, practiced every day and played the whole game after being inactive the week before.

signals.claim: Adebo is a top-level starting corner who played the whole game.
signals.note: Harbaugh strongly endorsed Adebo as a legitimate starting corner after a game ball performance, which should keep him in the lineup.
signals.quote: I think he's a legitimate corner in this league.

signals.claim: Carter broke out as a pass rusher with sacks, quarterback hits and 12 pressures.
signals.note: Carter's pass-rush production is trending up, and Harbaugh said he has been practicing at that level.

signals.claim: Banks played a great game and earned a game ball.
signals.note: Banks looks solid at corner opposite Adebo, which is good for the pass defense.
signals.quote: Both our corners played so well.

signals.note: Harbaugh said Thibodeaux's impact doesn't show up in the stats, so box-score production may understate his play.
signals.quote: Watch how physical he was and how hard he played.

signals.claim: Skattebo remains the ball carrier the team trusts in closing situations despite an earlier fumble.
signals.note: Harbaugh stuck with him late in the game and said he has been protecting the football, which points to continued lead-back work.
signals.quote: he was the guy to get back to.

signals.claim: The offense will keep taking deep shots and expects McCarthy to start connecting on them.
signals.note: McCarthy missed some deep throws and had trouble sustaining drives, but the coach backed him and the downfield plan, which adds upside for the receivers.
signals.quote: we're going to start hitting some of those deep passes.

signals.note: Fields made the key catch on the final drive on a throw Harbaugh called a needle-threading strike, which shows McCarthy trusts him in big moments.
signals.quote: That was a big time throw.

topics.detail: Harbaugh called the defensive performance remarkable against a high-powered offense. The line took away the run game, and one-on-one pass-rush wins pressured Trevor Lawrence.
The offense moved the ball when it avoided penalties but missed chances to put the game away early in the third quarter. Harbaugh pointed to a missed kick, no touchdown and a turnover.
Harbaugh praised Dennard Wilson as a great leader and defensive mind who keeps players accountable and has the unit locked in.
Harbaugh said the goal is to stack wins to win the division. He expects a very good, hungry opponent next week.

title: HC Aaron Glenn Postgame Press Conference (11/22) | Week 11
headline: Jets snap their losing streak with a balanced offense, Sterling Shepard's TD and Geno Smith's strong play; no new injuries and Geno's ankle is expected to be managed for next week.
summary: Aaron Glenn opened by saying the Jets got a win and came out of it with no injuries. He was pleased with the offense: the run game worked, the team was good in the red zone and on third down, and offensive coordinator Frank got credit for a strong game. Glenn said Frank called plays from the sideline this week, a change the two discussed earlier in the week, and that he wants to keep it because it worked. He conceded the defense still has to clean up third-down penalties. He called Sterling Shepard an 'Energizer bunny' who stays ready despite being inactive in recent weeks, and praised Geno Smith's comeback season, his preparation and his leadership. David Bailey drew high praise as a pressure player with close to ten sacks and several forced fumbles. Geno played through an ankle issue on adrenaline, and Glenn expects him to be sore but manageable for next week. Glenn also liked the balanced game plan in which eight different players caught passes and both Braelon Allen and Breece Hall had good games. He described next week as a holiday-week game.

injuries.detail: Played through an ankle injury; Glenn expects him to be a little sore but says the team will manage it and have him ready for next week.

signals.note: Shepard scored the touchdown that broke the team's TD drought after being inactive for weeks, but there is no stated plan for a bigger role.
signals.quote: he's been inactive, you know, all these weeks

signals.claim: Geno Smith will be managed through his ankle soreness and ready for next week's game.
signals.note: His ankle did not stop him from playing well or using his legs, so he looks on track as the starter next week.
signals.quote: he'll be sore a little bit, but we'll manage it

signals.note: Bailey is producing sacks and forced fumbles at a high rate and is a consistent big-play pass rusher, which is useful for IDP.
A reporter said Hall had a nice game in a balanced offense, and Glenn said the run game showed up as planned, which is encouraging for his workload. Glenn did not talk about Hall specifically.
A reporter said Allen had a nice game alongside Hall, so he may be sharing backfield work, but Glenn did not address it directly.

topics.detail: Offensive coordinator Frank called plays from the sideline for the first time, a plan he and Glenn discussed earlier in the week. Glenn plans to continue it because it helped the offense, and he can see the whole field and offer suggestions.
The run game worked, the red zone was productive and third down was good. Eight different players caught passes thanks to a game plan built to attack this specific opponent.
Glenn said the defense still has to improve, especially on third-down penalties, which he has been talking about for a while.
Next week is a holiday-week game, which Glenn called a big game for the team.
